copecks: small Russian coins, each worth a hundredth of a rouble
rouble: basic Russian unit of money, made up of a hundred copecks
roubles: Russian units of money, made up of a hundred copecks each
tavern: inn or drinking-house where people buy and drink alcohol
tavern-keeper: man who owns and runs a tavern or drinking-house
innkeeper: person who owns or manages an inn or tavern
garret: small, cheap room under the roof of a building
pomatum: scented ointment once used to smooth and shine the hair
concertina: small hand-held instrument like an accordion, played by squeezing bellows
kerchief: square cloth worn over the head or around the neck
shawl: large piece of cloth worn draped over the shoulders
pension: regular payment made to someone after they have retired from work
salary: fixed amount of money paid regularly for work done
counsellor: official holding a particular rank in the Russian civil service
titular: holding a title or rank without the real duties that usually go with it
clerk: office worker who keeps records, letters, and accounts
trifles: things of little importance or value
oaths: solemn promises, or angry swear words
crucified: tormented or made to suffer terribly, as if nailed to a cross
palate: sense of taste, or the roof of the mouth
palates: senses of taste, or the roofs of the mouth
verst: old Russian unit of distance, about one kilometre
candle-end: small leftover stub of a burned-down candle
honoured: respected, used as a formal title of respect in addresses
excellency: formal title of respect given to high officials or diplomats
poppet: term of affection, like darling or sweetheart
overstrained: worn out by working or worrying beyond normal limits
consumptive: suffering from consumption, an old name for tuberculosis
sniggering: snickering in a sly, suppressed way
jaunty: cheerful, lively, and self-confident in manner or appearance
waistcoat: sleeveless garment worn over a shirt, under a jacket
linen: underclothing, or bed sheets and cloths made from cloth
dames: old-fashioned term for ladies, especially of good social standing
pledge: item left with someone as security for a loan
reckoning: calculation of an amount owed, or settling of accounts
passers-by: people walking past on the street
entry: small entrance hall or passage inside a building
partitioned: divided into separate sections by thin walls
tinkle: light, high ringing sound, like a small bell
trunk: large strong box used for storing or carrying belongings
medal: small metal award given for service or bravery
crust: hard, dry outer surface of a loaf of bread
lodging: temporary place to live, often a rented room
barge: flat-bottomed boat used for carrying goods on rivers
gleamed: shone with a faint, soft light
counter: long bar or table in a tavern where drinks are served
sentiments: feelings, or opinions expressed about something
conceited: excessively proud of oneself and one's own abilities
prejudices: unfair opinions formed in advance without good reason
dread: deep fear or anxious worry about something to come
pondered: thought about something carefully and at length
e-he-he: sly, drawn-out chuckling sound expressing amusement or mockery
etrovitch: a patronymic, the father's name used as a middle name
ragged: torn, worn out, and shabby in appearance
cross: wooden or metal symbol of Christian faith, often worn around the neck
hungry: wanting food, having little or nothing to eat
